definitions.explanation: Not yet completed. Used for works of art, literature, projects, or tasks that remain unfinished.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{未完|みかん}のまま{終|お}わった。
{未完|みかん}の{作品|さくひん}が{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: An unfinished work is on display.

examples.japanese: {作者|さくしゃ}が{亡|な}くなったため、この{大作|たいさく}は{未完|みかん}に{終|お}わってしまった。
examples.english: Because the author passed away, this great work was left unfinished.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used as a modifier with の: {未完|みかん}の{作品|さくひん} (unfinished work). Also appears as a predicate or label: {未完|みかん}に{終|お}わる (to end incomplete). Common in literary and artistic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未完|みかん}の{作品|さくひん} (unfinished work)
- {未完|みかん}に{終|お}わる (to remain unfinished)
- {未完成|みかんせい} (incomplete — a related but distinct word meaning not yet perfected)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {未完成|みかんせい}: incomplete, not yet finished — implies something still in progress that could be completed
- {未完|みかん}: unfinished — often implies the work will never be completed
